## Quick note on factors

Factors are a datatype that converts a character into a ordinal datatype.
Think low medium and high

```{r}
library(NHSRdatasets)

data <- NHSRdatasets::ae_attendances

data <- data |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    attendance_grouping = dplyr::case_when(
      attendances < 5000 ~ 'Less than 5,000',
      attendances < 10000 ~ '5,000 to 9,999',
      attendances < 15000 ~ '10,000 to 14,999',
      attendances < 20000 ~ '15,000 to 19,999',
      attendances < 25000 ~ '20,000 to 24,999',
      attendances >= 25000 ~ '25,000 and over',
      .default = 'ERROR - does not compute'
    )
  )
```

## Look at our attendance groupings

```{r}
data_fact <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(period == '2016-04-01', 
                type == '1') |>
  dplyr::arrange(attendance_grouping)

data_fact
```


## Let's do a super quick plot

```{r}
data_fact |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = attendance_grouping)) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar()

```

## Character to factor data type

We can then make it ordinal:

```{r}
data_fact <- data_fact |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    attendance_grouping = factor(
      attendance_grouping,
      levels = c(
        "Less than 5,000",
        "5,000 to 9,999",
        "10,000 to 14,999",
        "15,000 to 19,999",
        "20,000 to 24,999",
        "25,000 and over"
      )
    )
  )

data_fact

```

## Let's do our plot again

```{r}
data_fact |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = attendance_grouping)) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar()

```

:::{.callout-warning collapse=false appearance='default' icon=true}
If you set your data as factors, R will not like you adding data
into that column if is not one of the factors you have created.

There are ways of doing this but don't have time now to go into detail
:::
